generation: Use case: scientific-educational. Make a transparent RGBA anatomy sprite sheet, FOUR separate isolated MUSCLE sprites in an EXACT TWO-column TWO-row grid on a 1024x1024 canvas. Reference image only for reddish-brown muscle fiber material and consistent diffuse upper-left lighting. This is a flexion VARIANT atlas for a real-time educational anatomy overlay. TOP LEFT: anatomical RIGHT upper-arm anterior muscle group, shoulder/deltoid at top, elbow tendon at bottom, no forearm, relaxed upper arm axis vertical; show biceps shortened and rounded with elbow flexed approximately 90 degrees but do not bend the upper arm itself. TOP RIGHT: anatomical LEFT upper arm, independent anatomy and same upper-left illumination, shoulder top elbow tendon bottom, same flexed biceps. BOTTOM LEFT: RIGHT anterior thigh quadriceps, hip top knee bottom, slightly rounded muscle bellies and clear patella/tendon when knee is flexed 60 degrees, no lower leg. BOTTOM RIGHT: LEFT anterior thigh quadriceps same knee-flexed state, independently rendered. Keep long axes perfectly vertical, all sprites same proximal-distal anchor proportions as reference, object centered within cell, 35px transparent margins, not cropped. Anatomically coherent individual volumes, no invented extra muscles, cream fascia/tendons, obvious parallel fiber direction and deep grooves. Realistic 3D museum anatomy render look, no blood or wounds, no skin, no text/labels, no floor/shadow, no checkerboard. Actual zero-alpha transparent background. Consistent color, soft light, and scale between both sides.
correction: Correct an anatomical error ONLY in the TOP TWO sprites of this atlas. They are upper arms, NOT thighs. Remove the erroneous round patella/kneecap-like white bone at the bottom of EACH of the top two upper-arm sprites. Upper arms must have NO kneecap, no round knee joint, no exposed ball-shaped bone distally. Replace that distal region with the tapering pale flat biceps tendon/aponeurosis and a narrow elbow termination, as a real anterior upper arm would have. Retain rounded flexed biceps muscle belly, deltoid at shoulder, directional muscle fibers. Keep the two BOTTOM quadriceps/knee sprites unchanged (kneecaps are correct there). Preserve cell positions, scale, overall canvas, realistic 3D texture, consistent lighting and actual transparent alpha background. No text. No extra parts. This atlas is for teaching anatomy and the two upper arms must never look like legs.
